subject: StratusAI performance escalation: RCA, remediation commitments & exec handoff
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: StratusAI — urgent: weekend throughput spike & 5xx increase

Team,

Quick summary of the weekend: StratusAI saw a sustained throughput spike between 02:00 and 08:00 UTC on Saturday (Dec 4) that coincided with a ~3.8% 5xx rate and median tail latency increase from 120ms to 560ms for their high-volume route (embed.batch_v2). They reached their Dedicated pool max and we started falling back to hosted model variants which amplified cold start latency.

Immediate asks:
- Jonas: RCA + timeline for root cause analysis and mitigations (priority: autoscaler behavior & cache thrash).
- Karthik: coordinate with Customer Success/commercial on top-level customer communication and potential credit ask.
- Marissa: prepare an exec-facing digest (ppt/pdf) we can share with StratusAI leadership by EOD Thu so we can lock in the readout.

Attachments we need: initial incident logs, autoscaler metrics, and a consolidated SLO gap snapshot. I pulled preliminary traces into the incident channel but we need a concise narrative.

This is already on the radar for the executive team — I expect an ask for a financial remediation estimate. Please treat as high priority.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: StratusAI — urgent: weekend throughput spike & 5xx increase

Evelyn — initial RCA and proposed mitigations below. I attached a draft RCA (stratusai-rca.pdf) and the action-tracker workbook.

Root cause (summary):
1) Autoscaler configuration: aggressive downscale threshold combined with prometheus scrape gaps caused the Dedicated pool to undershoot required capacity during a sustained traffic surge. Downscale triggered unnecessary preemption of long-lived inference workers.
2) KV cache thrash: prefix-skew in embedding keys during the spike increased KV cache misses, causing more frequent model context reloads and higher token generation overhead on fallback variants.
3) Fallback policy: hosted fallback model variant has longer cold-starts and different batching behavior; routing persisted for 47 minutes before we elevated capacity.

Immediate mitigations implemented (Dec 5-6):
- Reverted downscale aggressiveness (temporarily raised min replicas by +30% for StratusAI pool).
- Implemented a short-term cache-warmup hook on hot prefixes to reduce cold cache misses.
- Adjusted fallback policy to prefer warm standby variants and reduced fallback duration threshold from 10m -> 3m.

Outstanding corrective actions (tracked in action tracker):
A1) Autoscaler metrics -> implement heartbeat guard to ignore short scrape windows (owner: infra/ops) — ETA 72h.
A2) Long-term autoscale policy redesign with traffic-shift detection (owner: serving/runtime) — ETA 3 weeks.
A3) Model variant reconciliation: ensure warm standby images in every zone for critical customers (owner: infra) — ETA 2 weeks.
A4) Post-deploy canary for cache and batching changes (owner: platform) — ETA 1 week.

Impact to SLA/credits: pending commercial recommendation. I estimate the measurable SLA gap (tokens over SLO and error units) as 6.1% of December committed usage for the impacted routes — Marissa/Karthik, please advise commercial posture.

Next steps: I propose an exec readout on Thu 12/9 (US morning) to walk StratusAI through the RCA and the 3-week remediation plan.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: StratusAI exec handoff: RCA acceptance, approvals, and next 21 days (final)

Team / StratusAI execs,

Thanks to everyone for the quick turnaround on the RCA draft and for joining this morning's exec readout. This thread consolidates final commitments and approvals so we have a single source of truth.

Summary (accepted by StratusAI in the readout):
- Root cause: autoscaler downscale + cache thrash + fallback latency (as detailed in the RCA).
- Immediate mitigation status: min replicas increased, cache warmup in place, fallback policy tightened — these actions have reduced observed 5xx rates to <0.2% in the last 24h for the affected routes.

Committed remediation roadmap (owners & ETA):
- Week 1 (complete): autoscaler heartbeat guard + permanent min-replica policy for StratusAI (owner: infra) — DONE.
- Week 2 (in progress): canary and rollout of long-lived warm standby variants in all zones (owner: serving/runtime) — ETA 7 days.
- Week 3: autoscale policy redesign with traffic-shift detection and full regression tests (owner: platform) — ETA 21 days.

Commercial resolution (approved to send to procurement):
- One-time credit: 40% of estimated impacted route spend (~$38,000).
- Conditional protection clause: additional 20% credit if regression occurs within 90 days.
- Marissa will send formal credit terms & updated MSA amendment for signature (DocuSign link in related_links).

Operational follow-through (action tracker):
- I will own weekly status updates to StratusAI (cc: Jonas) until the week-3 milestone completes.
- Karthik/Marissa: confirm billing adjustment and coordinate procurement contact (DEAL-8791).

If anyone needs a separate exec sign-off or higher-level approval for a larger remediation envelope, call me directly — our recommended ceiling for credit without CEO approval is $50k.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
